label: Internal restlessness & cognitive disengagement
summary: Two measured constructs for the 'calm outside, churning inside' state: internalized hyperactivity (the restless pole) and cognitive disengagement syndrome (the foggy pole), and why they point to different differentials.

label: ADHD & anxiety — overlap, direction, and what tells them apart
summary: Why ADHD and anxiety produce the same internal state (high comorbidity, symptom overlap, emotional dysregulation) and what actually discriminates them — structure and onset rather than intensity.

label: The adult ADHD assessment — what a full evaluation involves
summary: What guideline-grade adult ADHD evaluation actually consists of (clinical interview, childhood history, collateral informants, impairment, ruling out mimics), why a self-report screen is the weakest tier, and what to bring to the appointment.

label: ADHD interventions — what works, and why response is not proof
summary: The evidence base for ADHD treatment — medication, CBT, mindfulness — and the diagnostic caution that a positive stimulant response does not confirm ADHD because it also helps people without it.

label: ADHD neurobiology & imaging — distributed networks, small effects
summary: What neurobiology has found — default-mode interference and distributed large-scale networks rather than a single locus — and why the structural-imaging differences are real but far too small (and in adults absent) to diagnose anyone.

label: Autism & ADHD overlap — co-occurrence, shared causes, distinct categories
summary: Why autism and ADHD overlap — high co-occurrence, shared heritability and neurocognition — and why they nonetheless stay distinct diagnostic categories, with the boundary question held open.

label: ADHD & sleep — mimic, consequence, or shared circadian clock
summary: Beyond sleep-as-rival: the ADHD–sleep link is bidirectional, delayed circadian phase is highly prevalent and may be intrinsic to a subgroup, and the mimic/consequence/shared-mechanism question is held open.

label: ADHD & mood — mimic, consequence, or shared liability
summary: Depression completes the differential: it co-occurs with ADHD, ADHD prospectively (and plausibly causally) raises depression risk, and the mimic/consequence/shared question is held open — with course (episodic vs chronic) the practical discriminator.

label: ADHD in women & girls — missed, harmed when missed, and hormone-modulated
summary: Beyond the skewed sex ratio: girls and women present more inattentively and get missed, the miss is costly (elevated self-harm), and symptom expression is modulated by reproductive hormones — a female-specific axis male-referenced models ignore.

label: ADHD & executive function — core deficit, one component, and the test–life gap
summary: The executive-function theory of ADHD (inhibition-centred), the meta-analytic nuance that EF deficits are neither necessary nor sufficient, the heterogeneity that follows, and why lab EF tests miss the real-world executive problems that ratings capture.

label: ADHD & rejection sensitivity — a real construct behind a popular label
summary: Separates the popular 'rejection sensitive dysphoria' label from the evidence: rejection sensitivity is a validated general construct and a plausible facet of ADHD's emotional dysregulation, but the RSD-as-ADHD-syndrome framing is under-evidenced and clinically risky.

label: ADHD & hyperfocus — the focus paradox as attention dysregulation
summary: The paradox that an 'attention deficit' can lock onto tasks intensely — reframed as dysregulated attention allocation (can't sustain, can't disengage); elevated in ADHD on new measures but poorly defined, non-specific, and non-diagnostic.

label: ADHD & time perception — timing deficits, "time blindness", and a contested marker
summary: ADHD is consistently impaired across timing domains and people describe time slipping away ('time blindness'); the deficit is real at the group level but non-specific, and its proposal as a diagnostic marker is held open.

label: ADHD & motivation — a reward-processing difference, not laziness
summary: Motivation as a third axis of ADHD: reduced dopamine reward-pathway function (Volkow), altered reinforcement sensitivity and contingency-dependent performance (Luman, Morsink) — reframing interest/urgency-driven performance as reward processing rather than a character flaw.

label: ADHD & working memory — a robust deficit, and the movement that helps it
summary: Working memory is one of ADHD's most robust deficits (larger for spatial, persists into adulthood); and objective work suggests movement can compensate — hyperactivity aiding working memory rather than only impairing it.

label: ADHD & sensory sensitivity — atypical, dimensional, and not only autism
summary: Sensory hyper- and hyposensitivity is elevated in ADHD, tracks ADHD traits dimensionally, and appears irrespective of autistic symptoms — an emerging, under-studied and transdiagnostic feature rather than a diagnostic sign.

label: ADHD comorbidity overview — the differential is usually "and", not "or"
summary: The synthesis over the differential notes: comorbidity is the rule in ADHD (most have a co-occurring disorder), substance use is elevated in both directions, and overlap means the clinical question is which conditions co-occur — treat the most impairing first.

label: ADHD & self-esteem — a consequence of accumulated failure, and a modifiable one
summary: Self-esteem is lower across the ADHD lifespan, built from years of negative feedback rather than intrinsic, part of the demoralization pathway toward depression — and it improves with treatment and support.

label: ADHD & relationships — strain on couples and families, and what carries it
summary: ADHD strains couple and family relationships — poorer marital adjustment, lower romantic relationship quality, higher divorce risk — mediated substantially by emotional dysregulation and conflict, and addressable through assessment and treatment.

label: ADHD & exercise — a modest, real, low-risk adjunct
summary: Aerobic exercise produces moderate improvements in core ADHD symptoms and executive function, acutely and chronically, plausibly via catecholamines; the effect is modest and dose-dependent, making it a low-risk adjunct rather than a replacement.

label: ADHD & diet — the sugar myth, and the small print on the rest
summary: The sugar-causes-hyperactivity belief is unsupported; elimination diets, omega-3 and food-color avoidance have small, subgroup-specific effects — diet is a low-risk adjunct with modest expectations, not a primary treatment.

label: ADHD & screen time — a small association, and an unresolved arrow
summary: The screen-media/ADHD association is statistically small across meta-analysis, review and prospective cohort, and causality is unresolved and plausibly bidirectional — the 'screens cause ADHD' claim outruns the evidence.

label: ADHD & procrastination — a self-regulation failure, not a scheduling one
summary: Procrastination is a near-universal but unnamed ADHD complaint, driven by inattention, and best understood as self-regulation and delay-discounting failure rather than poor time management — the same profile ADHD represents in the extreme.

label: ADHD & stigma — the "is it even real" problem, inside and out
summary: ADHD faces substantial lifelong stigma driven largely by public doubt about its validity; adults commonly internalize it, which adds to the burden and lowers self-esteem — a doubt the notebook’s own evidence base directly answers.

label: ADHD & sleep hygiene — fixing sleep as a lever on the symptoms
summary: Behavioural sleep intervention and sleep hygiene improve ADHD symptoms as well as sleep (guideline first-line), while melatonin advances a delayed sleep phase without directly treating ADHD — a low-risk, high-value lever given sleep's role in the differential.

label: ADHD & coping strategies — effortful compensation that works, with limits
summary: Coping strategies (routine, externalising, reframing, CBT skills) are evidence-based compensation that reduces ADHD symptoms — but they are effortful, cost extra work, and their long-term quality-of-life payoff is uneven.

label: ADHD & hormones — the lifelong interplay the male-referenced model misses
summary: Sex hormones regulate the signalling systems implicated in ADHD, so symptoms and cognition shift across the menstrual cycle and the female lifespan, and hormone-related mood disorders (PMDD, postpartum, climacteric) are elevated in women with ADHD.

label: ADHD & creativity — a real, trait-level, interest-driven edge, not a superpower
summary: ADHD's creativity link is real but nuanced: a divergent-thinking advantage at trait (not clinical) level and for idea generation only, with real-world achievement driven by goal-directed motivation in self-chosen domains — the 'superpower' framing overstates it.

label: ADHD & impulsivity — not one thing, and not ADHD-specific
summary: Impulsivity in ADHD is multidimensional — motor inhibition, choice/delay discounting and emotional urgency dissociate with different biology — and transdiagnostic, so it describes rather than distinguishes ADHD.
